correctness.rationale: Evaluation is injective by distinct character residues modulo q−1. A gcd polygon Q leaves the residual translate set R(Q). Here is an independent classification: by the hexagon symmetries any width-two direction among x,y,x+y can be taken to be x. It fixes the x translation; to permit three distinct y translations in the width-two hexagon, Q would need zero widths in y and x+y, impossible. With all three widths at most one, translate the x,y minima to zero. The unit square allows only horizontal, vertical and anti-diagonal primitive segments and the two triangles not spanning both (0,0) and (1,1). The strip constraints directly give residual unit parallelograms or unit triangles respectively. The segment gcd vanishes on q−1 torus points and the residual Segre map is injective, so three residual sections have at most one further common zero and four have none. A triangle contributes q−2 points and its full residual space has no common zero. If there is no common Laurent factor, choose two generic combinations over the algebraic closure without a shared torus curve (a common geometric factor would descend by taking its conjugate orbit). The isolated-torus mixed-area bound is six, sufficient for q≥7; the alternative projective wording 'length six' should not be read literally if boundary components are fixed. For q=5 multiplication by a torus element scales evaluation columns and lets one normalize a point to (1,1). Independent column-space elimination gives minima four and five over all 1365 normalized five-point and 3003 normalized six-point sets. For sharpness, the whole residual space for x−a gives precisely the fiber; its kernel of evaluation at an off-fiber point gives that point and the fiber. For r≥5, any three distinct rows are independent via Vandermonde on distinct x or y, or the columns 1,x,y when precisely two x coordinates agree. Thus the five maxima and weights follow.
residual_risks: The geometric bound is for isolated points in the torus, not a claim that every pair of sections intersects properly on the projective boundary. The stated ruling examples show attainment; no classification of all extremizers is used.

value.rationale: The generalized weights describe linear-section incidence of a natural toric evaluation embedding. The sharp change from a fiber plus one point to a fiber alone is useful information beyond the ordinary distance and d₂, and the all-field result resolves the genuine small-field gap in the intersection bound. The elementary last three weights complete the remaining hierarchy.
residual_risks: No implication for projective-surface evaluation, nonsplit surfaces, or fields below five.
